state: Can's authored TypeScript runs on Bun 1.4.2. Oxlint 1.85.0 currently reports 73 warnings across runtime/ and tools/runtime/ after excluding vendored code: 48 no-unused-vars, 11 no-new-array, 6 no-control-regex, 5 no-thenable, 2 no-useless-spread, and 1 no-this-alias. The user requests a sound plan to eliminate all warnings. Tests intentionally create thenable-shaped hostile objects; some new Array(n) calls create sparse arrays or length-driven output; regexes match forbidden control bytes; spread copies can be ownership boundaries. The repository requires preserving Can contracts and immutability, using native JS/Bun operations, and has no external compatibility obligation. Potential strategies are local semantic repairs with narrow justified rule suppressions, blanket rule disabling, or mechanical changes for every warning. Oxlint's --deny-warnings can make a clean baseline a gate. The plan itself should avoid editing runtime behavior before review.

resolution.instructions: Which remediation policy should the warning plan use when a warning identifies deliberate behavior?

criteria.targeted: Inspect each site; repair genuine dead code and ambiguity; retain deliberate semantics through precise expressions or narrow documented suppressions after evidence.
criteria.global_disable: Disable whole rules or directories when several findings are intentional, and repair only remaining findings.
criteria.mechanical: Rewrite all flagged code into Oxlint-preferred forms even when the original idiom may encode sparse arrays, hostile getters, or ownership copies.

gate.instructions: What enforcement sequence best fits a plan for all 73 warnings?

criteria.finish_then_gate: Resolve every warning, verify focused behavior and full runtime tests, then enable --deny-warnings for scoped authored TypeScript.
criteria.gate_first: Enable --deny-warnings immediately and work under a failing lint gate until all fixes land.
criteria.no_gate: Clear the current list once and leave future warnings nonblocking.
